4.	In 1930, sixteen-year-old George Nissen of Cedar Rapids, Iowa was watching trapeze artists at a circus when he got the idea for an invention. He built a prototype in his garage using angle iron and canvas and began performing with it. Nissen went on to win the AAU national tumbling championship three years in a row and represented the United States in gymnastics at the X Olympics. After returning home, he and his gymnastics coach Larry Griswold co-founded a company and began manufacturing the apparatus commercially. To name it, Nissen drew on his limited Spanish and used the word for a diving board. He was a relentless promoter of Y as a sport and showman throughout his life: in a famous 1965 publicity stunt, he arranged to bounce on a Y with a kangaroo to generate press coverage. Y became an Olympic event at the Sydney Games in 2000, sixty years after Nissen first began manufacturing them. ID X (5 points) and Y (10 points).
